source.text: Ὦ ἀνόητοι Γαλάται, τίς ὑμᾶς ἐβάσκανεν, οἷς κατ’ ὀφθαλμοὺς Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς προεγράφη ἐσταυρωμένος;

records.literal_gloss: O foolish Galatians, who you bewitched, to whom before eyes Jesus Christ was publicly portrayed having been crucified?

en.L: O foolish Galatians, who has bewitched you, before whose eyes Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} was publicly portrayed as crucified?
en.B: You foolish Galatians! Who has put you under a spell? Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} was set out in full view before your eyes as the crucified one.
en.R: You foolish people of Galatia! Who has put a spell on you? It was made so plain to you that Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} was crucified. It was as if you had seen it with your own eyes.

es.L: ¡Oh gálatas insensatos! ¿Quién {{plural_you:los|os}} hechizó, a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, ante cuyos ojos {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías,}} fue presentado públicamente como crucificado?
es.B: ¡Gálatas insensatos! ¿Quién {{plural_you:los|os}} ha hechizado? Ante {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} ojos se expuso a plena vista a {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías,}} como el crucificado.
es.R: ¡Gálatas, qué insensatos {{plural_you:son|sois}}! ¿Quién {{plural_you:los|os}} ha engañado como con un hechizo? Se {{plural_you:les|os}} mostró con mucha claridad que {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías,}} fue crucificado. Fue como si lo {{plural_you:hubieran|hubierais}} visto con {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} propios ojos.

sw.L: Enyi Wagalatia msiotumia akili, ni nani amewaroga, ninyi ambao mbele ya macho yenu Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} alionyeshwa hadharani kuwa amesulubiwa?
sw.B: Enyi Wagalatia msiotumia akili! Ni nani amewaroga? Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} aliwekwa wazi mbele ya macho yenu kama yule aliyesulubiwa.
sw.R: Ninyi watu wa Galatia, hamtumii akili zenu! Ni nani aliyewapotosha kana kwamba amewaroga? Mlielezwa waziwazi kwamba Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} alisulubiwa. Ilikuwa kana kwamba mliona kwa macho yenu wenyewe.

fr.L: Ô Galates irréfléchis, qui vous a ensorcelés, vous aux yeux de qui Jésus {{christos:Christ|Messie}} a été dépeint publiquement comme crucifié ?
fr.B: Galates irréfléchis ! Qui vous a jeté un sort ? Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}} a pourtant été exposé en pleine lumière sous vos yeux, comme le crucifié.
fr.R: Habitants de la Galatie, comme vous manquez de bon sens ! Qui vous a jeté un sort ? On vous a montré si clairement que Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}} a été crucifié ! C’était comme si vous l’aviez vu de vos propres yeux.

ko.L: 어리석은 갈라디아 사람들이여, 누가 여러분을 홀렸습니까? 여러분의 눈앞에 예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}께서 십자가에 못 박히신 분으로 공공연히 그려졌는데도 [말입니다].
ko.B: 어리석은 갈라디아 사람들이여! 누가 여러분을 홀렸습니까? 예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}께서 십자가에 못 박히신 분으로 여러분의 눈앞에 똑똑히 드러났는데도 말입니다.
ko.R: 어리석은 갈라디아 사람들이여! 누가 여러분에게 마술을 걸었습니까? 예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}께서 십자가에 못 박히셨다는 사실이 여러분에게 아주 분명하게 전해졌습니다. 마치 여러분이 그것을 직접 눈으로 본 것 같았습니다.

vi.L: Ôi những người Ga-la-ti dại dột, ai đã mê hoặc anh chị em, là những người đã được thấy Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}} bị đóng đinh trên thập tự giá được bày ra công khai trước mắt mình?
vi.B: Anh chị em Ga-la-ti thật thiếu suy nghĩ! Ai đã bỏ bùa mê anh chị em? Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}} đã được bày ra rõ ràng trước mắt anh chị em như Đấng chịu đóng đinh trên thập tự giá.
vi.R: Anh chị em ở Ga-la-ti thật thiếu suy nghĩ! Ai đã bỏ bùa anh chị em vậy? Anh chị em đã được cho thấy thật rõ ràng rằng Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}} đã bị đóng đinh trên thập tự giá. Điều đó rõ như thể chính mắt anh chị em đã thấy.

pt.L: Ó gálatas insensatos, quem enfeitiçou vocês, diante de cujos olhos Jesus {{christos:Cristo|Messias}} foi exposto publicamente como crucificado?
pt.B: Gálatas insensatos! Quem lançou um feitiço sobre vocês? Jesus {{christos:Cristo|o Messias}} foi apresentado diante dos olhos de vocês, à vista de todos, como o crucificado.
pt.R: Gente da Galácia, como vocês estão sendo tolos! Quem colocou um feitiço em vocês? Ficou muito claro para vocês que Jesus {{christos:Cristo|o Messias}} foi crucificado. Foi como se vocês tivessem visto isso com os próprios olhos.

am.L: እናንት የማታስተውሉ ገላትያውያን ሆይ፣ ኢየሱስ {{christos:ክርስቶስ|መሲሕ}} እንደ ተሰቀለ በዓይኖቻችሁ ፊት በግልጥ ተሥሎ የቀረበላችሁ እናንተን ማን ደገመባችሁ?
am.B: እናንት የማታስተውሉ ገላትያውያን! ማን አስማት አደረገባችሁ? ኢየሱስ {{christos:ክርስቶስ|መሲሕ}} የተሰቀለው እርሱ እንደ ሆነ በዓይኖቻችሁ ፊት በግልጥ ቀርቦላችሁ ነበር።
am.R: እናንተ የማታስተውሉ የገላትያ ሰዎች! ማን አስማት አደረገባችሁ? ኢየሱስ {{christos:ክርስቶስ|መሲሕ}} እንደ ተሰቀለ በግልጥ ተነግሯችሁ ነበር። በገዛ ዓይናችሁ ያያችሁት ያህል ነበር።

decisions.choice: foolish: failing to think, not lacking intelligence
decisions.reason: ἀνόητος describes people who do not use the understanding they have. Paul is not insulting their minds; he is shocked that they have not thought through what they already know. He repeats the word in verse 3.

decisions.choice: bewitched: a figure of speech for being led astray as if by a spell
alternatives: a claim that real sorcery was used
decisions.reason: βασκαίνω was used of casting a spell, often through the "evil eye" that people of the time feared. Paul uses it as an image: the change in the Galatians is so strange that it looks as though someone has put them under a spell. The image fits the "eyes" that follow: they had seen Christ crucified, yet someone has drawn their gaze away.

decisions.choice: publicly portrayed: set before them as plainly as a public notice
alternatives: written about beforehand, as in the prophets
decisions.reason: προγράφω was used of notices posted in public. Paul's preaching had made the crucifixion so vivid that it was as though they saw it. The same verb can mean "written beforehand" (Romans 15:4), but "before your eyes" points to a public display, not to prophecy.

decisions.choice: crucified: Christ remains the crucified one
alternatives: a reference only to the past event
decisions.reason: ἐσταυρωμένος is a perfect participle: the crucifixion happened once, but its effect stands, and Christ is presented as the one who was crucified. Everything Paul argues in this chapter rests on what the cross did (verse 13).

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} (L); {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: put you under a spell; set out in full view; as if you had seen it with your own eyes (R)
decisions.reason: "Bewitched" is an old-fashioned word, so Balanced and Readable use "spell". Readable breaks the sentence and explains the picture of a public display (meaning note m3).

decisions.choice: ustedes / vosotros forms
decisions.reason: Paul writes to the Galatian churches in the plural throughout the letter. As in Romans, each plural "you" and its verb is a reader setting: ustedes (Latin America, the default) or vosotros (Spain).

decisions.choice: insensatos
decisions.reason: "Insensatos" are people who act without good sense, which is what the meaning decision describes: they are failing to think, not lacking intelligence. "Tontos" would say they are slow-witted. The same word returns in verse 3.

decisions.choice: msiotumia akili (L, B); hamtumii akili zenu (R)
decisions.reason: "Wajinga" (ignorant) and "wapumbavu" (stupid) would insult their minds, and "msio na akili" says they have no sense at all. The meaning decision says Paul is shocked that they are not using the understanding they have, so Swahili says "msiotumia akili", you who do not use your minds. Verse 3 keeps the same picture.

decisions.choice: irréfléchis (L, B); comme vous manquez de bon sens (R); the same in 3:3
decisions.reason: The word describes people who do not use the understanding they have, not people lacking intelligence (m1). "Irréfléchis" says exactly that; "insensés" now suggests madness and "stupides" an insult to their minds.

decisions.choice: jeter un sort (B, R); ensorceler (L)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the verb of witchcraft; Balanced and Readable use the everyday expression for the same picture (m2).

decisions.choice: "어리석은 갈라디아 사람들이여" at every level
decisions.reason: Paul breaks off into an exclamation. The vocative "-이여" is no longer used for ordinary address (the letter says "여러분"), but it is still the natural Korean form for a cry of reproach like this, and it keeps the force of the Greek "O".

decisions.choice: "홀리다" (L, B); "마술을 걸다" (R)
decisions.reason: The verb is a figure of speech for being led astray as if under a spell (the meaning decision). "홀리다" (to bewitch, to captivate) keeps the picture in plain Korean; Readable uses the everyday "마술을 걸다", as the English Readable says "put a spell on you".

decisions.choice: "Ôi những người Ga-la-ti dại dột" (L); "Anh chị em Ga-la-ti thật thiếu suy nghĩ!" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek is a sharp cry of address. "Hỡi" belongs to older speech, so Literal says "Ôi" and Balanced and Readable make it a statement to the readers, keeping "anh chị em". The word is failing to think, not lack of intelligence (m1), so Balanced and Readable say "thiếu suy nghĩ"; "ngu muội" would insult their minds.

decisions.choice: "mê hoặc" (L); "bỏ bùa mê" (B), "bỏ bùa" (R)
decisions.reason: The verb is a figure of speech for a spell (m2). Vietnamese has the same picture in "bỏ bùa", which keeps it plain.

decisions.choice: insensatos (L, B); tolos (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book, as for "fool" in the other letters: "insensato" is someone who does not use the sense he has, which is what m1 describes; Readable says the everyday "tolo". "Burro" would insult their minds, which Paul does not do. The same in verse 3.

decisions.choice: enfeitiçou vocês
decisions.reason: "Enfeitiçar" is still ordinary Portuguese, unlike the English "bewitch", so Literal keeps the verb; Balanced and Readable say "lançar/colocar um feitiço", as the English says "put a spell".

decisions.choice: የማታስተውሉ (who do not think things through)
decisions.reason: Paul's word means failing to use one's mind, not lacking intelligence (meaning decision m1). "የማታስተውሉ" says that; "ሞኞች" and "ደደቦች" are insults about a person's wits.

source.text: τοῦτο μόνον θέλω μαθεῖν ἀφ’ ὑμῶν, ἐξ ἔργων νόμου τὸ πνεῦμα ἐλάβετε ἢ ἐξ ἀκοῆς πίστεως;

records.literal_gloss: This only I want to learn from you: by works of law the Spirit did you receive, or by hearing of faith?

en.L: This only I want to learn from you: did you receive the Spirit by works of [the] law, or by [the] hearing of faith?
en.B: Tell me just this one thing: did you receive the Spirit by works of the law, or by faith in what you heard?
en.R: I want you to answer just one question. Did you receive the Spirit because you did what the law commands? Or was it because you heard the message and put your faith in it?

es.L: Solo esto quiero saber de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}: ¿{{plural_you:recibieron|recibisteis}} el Espíritu por [las] obras de [la] ley, o por [el] oír de [la] fe?
es.B: {{plural_you:Díganme|Decidme}} solo esto: ¿{{plural_you:recibieron|recibisteis}} el Espíritu por las obras de la ley, o por la fe en lo que {{plural_you:oyeron|oísteis}}?
es.R: Solo {{plural_you:les|os}} quiero hacer una pregunta. ¿{{plural_you:Recibieron|Recibisteis}} el Espíritu porque {{plural_you:hicieron|hicisteis}} lo que la ley manda? ¿O fue porque {{plural_you:oyeron|oísteis}} el mensaje y {{plural_you:pusieron|pusisteis}} {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} fe en él?

sw.L: Hili tu nataka kujifunza kutoka kwenu: je, mlimpokea Roho kwa matendo ya sheria, au kwa kusikia kwa imani?
sw.B: Niambieni jambo hili moja tu: je, mlimpokea Roho kwa matendo ya sheria, au kwa kuamini kile mlichosikia?
sw.R: Nataka mnijibu swali moja tu. Je, mlimpokea Roho kwa sababu mlifanya yale ambayo sheria inaamuru? Au ni kwa sababu mlisikia ujumbe, mkauamini?

fr.L: Je veux seulement apprendre ceci de vous : est-ce par les œuvres de la Loi que vous avez reçu l’Esprit, ou par l’écoute de la foi ?
fr.B: Dites-moi seulement une chose : avez-vous reçu l’Esprit par les œuvres de la Loi, ou par la foi en ce que vous avez entendu ?
fr.R: Répondez seulement à une question. Avez-vous reçu l’Esprit parce que vous avez fait ce que la Loi ordonne ? Ou bien parce que vous avez entendu le message et que vous y avez cru ?

ko.L: 나는 여러분에게서 이것 하나만 알고 싶습니다. 여러분이 성령을 받은 것은 율법의 행위들로입니까, 아니면 믿음의 들음으로입니까?
ko.B: 한 가지만 말해 보십시오. 여러분이 성령을 받은 것은 율법의 행위 때문입니까, 아니면 들은 말씀을 믿었기 때문입니까?
ko.R: 한 가지만 물어보겠습니다. 여러분이 성령을 받은 것은 율법이 명령하는 것을 행했기 때문입니까? 아니면 기쁜 소식을 듣고 그것을 믿었기 때문입니까?

vi.L: Tôi chỉ muốn biết điều này từ anh chị em: anh chị em đã nhận lãnh Thánh Linh bởi những việc làm của luật pháp, hay bởi sự nghe với đức tin?
vi.B: Hãy cho tôi biết một điều thôi: anh chị em đã nhận lãnh Thánh Linh nhờ làm những việc luật pháp đòi hỏi, hay nhờ tin vào điều anh chị em đã nghe?
vi.R: Tôi chỉ muốn anh chị em trả lời một câu hỏi. Có phải anh chị em đã nhận lãnh Thánh Linh vì đã làm theo những gì luật pháp truyền dạy không? Hay là vì anh chị em đã nghe sứ điệp và đặt đức tin nơi sứ điệp ấy?

pt.L: Só isto quero saber de vocês: vocês receberam o Espírito por obras da Lei, ou pelo ouvir da fé?
pt.B: Digam-me só uma coisa: vocês receberam o Espírito pelas obras da Lei, ou pela fé naquilo que ouviram?
pt.R: Quero que vocês respondam só uma pergunta. Vocês receberam o Espírito porque fizeram o que a Lei manda? Ou foi porque ouviram a mensagem e puseram a sua fé nela?

am.L: ይህን ብቻ ከእናንተ ልማር እወዳለሁ፤ መንፈስን የተቀበላችሁት ከሕግ ሥራ ነውን ወይስ ከእምነት መስማት?
am.B: ይህን አንድ ነገር ብቻ ንገሩኝ፤ መንፈስን የተቀበላችሁት በሕግ ሥራ ነው ወይስ የሰማችሁትን በማመን?
am.R: ለአንድ ጥያቄ ብቻ መልስ እንድትሰጡኝ እፈልጋለሁ። መንፈስን የተቀበላችሁት ሕጉ የሚለውን ስላደረጋችሁ ነው? ወይስ መልእክቱን ሰምታችሁ ስላመናችሁበት ነው?

decisions.choice: the Spirit: God's Holy Spirit, given to them when they first believed
decisions.reason: Paul appeals to what the Galatians experienced: they received the Spirit of God (4:6) at the start of their life as believers. That gift is his evidence that God had already accepted them before anyone asked them to keep the law.

decisions.choice: works of the law: doing what the law of Moses requires
alternatives: only the ceremonial parts of the law
decisions.reason: The law is the law God gave through Moses. In this letter the question is above all circumcision, the food laws and the special days (2:3, 2:12, 4:10), the practices that marked Jews out from Gentiles, but Paul's argument covers keeping the law as a whole (3:10, 5:3).

decisions.choice: hearing with faith: they heard the message and believed it
alternatives: the message that calls for faith
decisions.reason: ἀκοή can mean the act of hearing or the message heard, and πίστις can mean the believer's faith or the content believed. So the phrase may mean "hearing accompanied by faith" or "the message that brings faith". Either way the contrast is between doing what the law requires and receiving God's message by believing it. We take the first, which matches "Abraham believed" in verse 6, and give the other in a footnote.

decisions.choice: works of [the] law (L); works of the law (B); doing what the law commands (R)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep Paul's phrase so the reader can follow it through the letter. Readable says plainly what it refers to.

decisions.choice: faith in what you heard (B); heard the message and put your faith in it (R)
decisions.reason: "Hearing of faith" is not natural English. Balanced and Readable give the sense chosen in meaning note m3 and keep the key word "faith".

decisions.choice: obras de la ley
decisions.reason: The phrase runs through the letter (2:16; 3:5, 10), so Literal and Balanced keep it in the same form each time, as in Romans 3. "Ley" is lowercase, like "law" in the English.

decisions.choice: matendo ya sheria
decisions.reason: As in Romans 3, "matendo" (deeds) says that these are things done in obedience to the law; "kazi" would suggest labour or a job. The phrase keeps this form through the letter.

decisions.choice: mlisikia ujumbe, mkauamini
decisions.reason: Swahili says "put your faith in it" most naturally with the verb "kuamini", which is the settled verb for believing and the same root as "imani".

decisions.choice: l'écoute de la foi (L); la foi en ce que vous avez entendu (B); vous avez entendu le message et vous y avez cru (R); the same in 3:5
decisions.reason: Literal keeps Paul's short phrase, which can mean hearing joined with faith or the message that brings faith (m3); "écoute" leaves both open. Balanced and Readable give the sense the English chose.

decisions.choice: "믿음의 들음" (L); "들은 말씀을 믿었기 때문" (B); "기쁜 소식을 듣고 그것을 믿었기 때문" (R), here and in verse 5
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek's two nouns, "hearing" and "faith"; the meaning decision reads them as hearing the message and believing it, which Balanced and Readable say.

decisions.choice: "Thánh Linh" for the Spirit, capitalised, through the letter
decisions.reason: The Spirit is God's Holy Spirit (m1), written as in the Vietnamese Colossians (1:8) and Romans.

decisions.choice: "sự nghe với đức tin" (L)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the phrase as hearing with faith (m3). "Sự nghe của đức tin" is not Vietnamese; "với" keeps the two nouns and their link.

decisions.choice: ከእምነት መስማት (from [the] hearing of faith)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps Paul's compact phrase, set against "ከሕግ ሥራ" with the same "ከ-" as the Greek repeats "by"; Balanced and Readable say what it means, believing what they heard (meaning decision m3).

en.R: How can you be so foolish?

sw.B: Je, kweli hamtumii akili kiasi hicho?

fr.R: Comment pouvez-vous manquer à ce point de bon sens ?

ko.R: 어떻게 여러분이 그렇게 어리석을 수 있습니까?

vi.L: Anh chị em dại dột đến thế sao?
vi.B: Anh chị em thật sự thiếu suy nghĩ đến thế sao?
vi.R: Sao anh chị em có thể thiếu suy nghĩ đến thế?

pt.R: Como vocês podem ser tão tolos?

decisions.choice: a question of astonishment
decisions.reason: The question expects no answer. With οὕτως ("so") Paul repeats the word "foolish" from verse 1 and voices his amazement at what they are doing.

records.literal_gloss: Having begun in Spirit, now in flesh are you being completed?

en.L: Having begun by [the] Spirit, are you now being brought to completion by [the] flesh?
en.B: You made your start by the Spirit; are you now going to reach the goal by the flesh?
en.R: You began your new life by the Spirit. Do you now think you can finish it by your own human effort?

es.L: Habiendo comenzado por [el] Espíritu, ¿ahora {{plural_you:están|estáis}} siendo llevados a término por [la] carne?
es.B: {{plural_you:Comenzaron|Comenzasteis}} por el Espíritu; ¿ahora {{plural_you:van|vais}} a llegar a la meta por el esfuerzo humano?
es.R: {{plural_you:Comenzaron|Comenzasteis}} {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} nueva vida por el Espíritu. ¿Ahora {{plural_you:creen|creéis}} que {{plural_you:pueden|podéis}} terminarla con {{plural_you:sus|vuestras}} propias fuerzas humanas?

sw.L: Mkiwa mmeanza kwa Roho, je, sasa mnakamilishwa kwa mwili?
sw.B: Mlianza kwa Roho; je, sasa mtafikia lengo kwa juhudi za kibinadamu?
sw.R: Mlianza maisha yenu mapya kwa Roho. Je, sasa mnadhani mnaweza kuyamaliza kwa juhudi zenu wenyewe za kibinadamu?

fr.L: Ayant commencé par l’Esprit, êtes-vous maintenant menés à l’achèvement par la chair ?
fr.B: Vous avez commencé par l’Esprit ; allez-vous maintenant atteindre le but par la chair ?
fr.R: Vous avez commencé votre vie nouvelle par l’Esprit. Pensez-vous maintenant pouvoir la terminer par vos propres efforts humains ?

ko.L: 성령으로 시작하였다가 이제는 육신으로 완성되려고 합니까?
ko.B: 성령으로 시작했는데, 이제는 육신으로 끝을 맺으려고 합니까?
ko.R: 여러분은 성령으로 새 삶을 시작했습니다. 그런데 이제는 여러분 자신의 힘으로 그 삶을 끝까지 이룰 수 있다고 생각합니까?

vi.L: Đã bắt đầu bởi Thánh Linh, nay anh chị em lại được làm cho trọn bởi xác thịt sao?
vi.B: Anh chị em đã khởi đầu bởi Thánh Linh, nay lại muốn đạt đến đích bằng xác thịt sao?
vi.R: Anh chị em đã bắt đầu đời sống mới nhờ Thánh Linh. Bây giờ anh chị em lại nghĩ rằng mình có thể hoàn tất đời sống ấy bằng sức riêng của con người sao?

pt.L: Tendo começado pelo Espírito, agora estão sendo levados à perfeição pela carne?
pt.B: Vocês começaram pelo Espírito; agora vão chegar ao fim pela carne?
pt.R: Vocês começaram a nova vida pelo Espírito. Agora acham que podem terminá-la com o próprio esforço humano?

am.B: በመንፈስ ጀመራችሁ፤ አሁን በሥጋ ወደ ግብ ልትደርሱ ነውን?
am.R: አዲሱን ሕይወታችሁን የጀመራችሁት በመንፈስ ነው። አሁን ደግሞ በራሳችሁ ሰብአዊ ጥረት ልትፈጽሙት የምትችሉ ይመስላችኋልን?

decisions.choice: flesh: human effort, what people can do in their own strength
decisions.reason: Set against the Spirit, σάρξ here means human beings acting on their own, without God. Paul is thinking of circumcision, a rite performed on the body, and of law-keeping as the way to complete their standing with God (6:12-13). Later in the letter the same word means the sinful human self (5:16-24).

decisions.choice: by the Spirit, by the flesh: the means by which the life is begun and finished
alternatives: in the sphere of the Spirit and of the flesh
decisions.reason: The two nouns stand without a preposition and say how each stage is brought about. Paul's question is whether the life the Spirit began can be completed by a different power.

decisions.choice: brought to completion: reaching the goal of the Christian life
decisions.reason: ἐπιτελέω means to bring something to its end or goal. Its form can be read as passive ("are you being completed") or as middle ("are you completing it"); the sense is the same. The contrast with "begun" shows that Paul has the whole course of their life with God in view.

decisions.choice: your new life; your own human effort
decisions.reason: Readable names what was begun and says what "flesh" means here (meaning note m1).

decisions.choice: carne (L); el esfuerzo humano (B); sus propias fuerzas humanas (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "carne", the settled word. The meaning decision reads it here as human effort, people acting in their own strength, and Spanish "carne" on its own is usually heard as the body or sexual desire, so Balanced says "el esfuerzo humano", where the English Balanced keeps "flesh". Readable says the same more plainly. Later in the letter (5:13-6:8) the word has a different sense and a different rendering.

decisions.choice: mwili (L); juhudi za kibinadamu (B); juhudi zenu wenyewe za kibinadamu (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "mwili", the settled word. The meaning decision reads it here as human effort, not the sinful self, so Balanced and Readable say "juhudi za kibinadamu" (human effort), where the English Balanced keeps "flesh". "Asili ya dhambi" is kept for 5:13-6:8, where the meaning is the sinful nature.

decisions.choice: la chair (L, B) for the whole letter; Readable says what it means in each place ("vos propres efforts humains" here, "ce corps humain" in 2:20, "vos désirs mauvais" in chapter 5)
decisions.reason: As in Colossians and Hebrews, Literal and Balanced keep "chair" so that the reader can follow the word through the letter, where its sense moves from bodily life (2:20) to human effort (here) and the sinful self (5:16-24).

decisions.choice: "육신" (L, B); "여러분 자신의 힘" (R)
decisions.reason: "육신" is the letter's word for the flesh at Literal and, where Paul sets it against the Spirit, at Balanced, as in Romans 8. Here it means human effort (the meaning decision), which Readable says, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "xác thịt" (L, B); "sức riêng của con người" (R) for sarx
decisions.reason: Here flesh is human effort, what people can do in their own strength (m1). Literal and Balanced keep "xác thịt", the word kept for sarx through the letter, set against the Spirit as Paul sets them; Readable says what it means, as the English Readable does.

records.literal_gloss: So many things did you experience in vain?

en.L: Did you experience so many things in vain?
en.B: Did you go through so much for nothing?
en.R: Have all the things that happened to you been for nothing?

es.R: ¿Todo lo que {{plural_you:les|os}} ha pasado ha sido para nada?

sw.L: Je, mlipitia mambo mengi hivyo bure?
sw.B: Je, mlipitia mambo mengi kiasi hicho bure?
sw.R: Je, mambo yote yaliyowapata yamekuwa bure?

fr.L: Avez-vous vécu tant de choses en vain ?
fr.B: Avez-vous vécu tout cela pour rien ?
fr.R: Est-ce que tout ce qui vous est arrivé n’a servi à rien ?

ko.L: 여러분이 그렇게 많은 것을 헛되이 겪었습니까?
ko.B: 여러분이 그 많은 일을 겪은 것이 헛일이었습니까?
ko.R: 여러분에게 일어난 그 모든 일이 다 헛된 것이었습니까?

vi.L: Anh chị em đã trải qua bao nhiêu điều như thế cách vô ích sao?
vi.B: Anh chị em đã trải qua biết bao điều mà chẳng được gì sao?
vi.R: Tất cả những điều đã xảy ra cho anh chị em đều là vô ích sao?

pt.B: Vocês passaram por tanta coisa à toa?
pt.R: Será que tudo o que aconteceu com vocês foi à toa?

am.R: ያጋጠማችሁ ነገር ሁሉ ከንቱ ሆኖ ቀረን?

decisions.choice: experienced: all they went through as believers, good and hard
decisions.reason: πάσχω usually means to suffer, and the Galatians may have been persecuted when they believed. But the verses around it speak of the Spirit and of miracles (verses 2-5), not of persecution, and the letter never mentions their suffering. So it may mean "experience" in a good sense. Both senses fit what Paul is asking: has all of it been wasted?

decisions.choice: experience (L); go through (B); things that happened to you (R)
decisions.reason: These words leave room for both readings in meaning note m1.

decisions.choice: experimentar (L); pasar por (B); lo que les ha pasado (R)
decisions.reason: "Padecer", the older wording, says only that they suffered. The meaning decision leaves room for good experiences as well, so Spanish uses verbs that cover both.

decisions.choice: kupitia (L, B); mambo yaliyowapata (R)
decisions.reason: "Kuteseka" would say only that they suffered. The meaning decision leaves room for good experiences as well, so Swahili says "kupitia mambo" (go through things) and Readable "mambo yaliyowapata" (the things that happened to you).

decisions.choice: vécu (L, B); tout ce qui vous est arrivé (R)
decisions.reason: The verb can mean suffering or experience in a good sense (m1). "Souffrir" would settle it for the first; "vivre" leaves both open, as the English does.

decisions.choice: experimentaram (L); passaram por (B); aconteceu com vocês (R)
decisions.reason: The verb usually means "suffer", but here it may mean all they went through (m1); these words leave both readings open, as the English does. "Sofreram" would decide for one.

decisions.choice: አሳለፋችሁ (you went through), ያጋጠማችሁ (what happened to you, R)
decisions.reason: The verb can mean suffering, but here it covers all they went through as believers, good and hard (meaning decision m1). "አሳለፈ" leaves both open, as "መከራ" (suffering) would not.

en.B: If it really was for nothing.
en.R: I hope it was not all for nothing!

es.L: Si es que de verdad [fue] en vano.
es.B: Si es que realmente fue para nada.
es.R: ¡Espero que no haya sido todo para nada!

fr.R: J’espère que ce n’était pas pour rien !

ko.R: 나는 그것이 모두 헛된 일이 아니었기를 바랍니다!

vi.B: Nếu điều đó thật là vô ích.
vi.R: Tôi mong rằng không phải tất cả đều vô ích!

pt.L: Se é que [foi] mesmo em vão.
pt.B: Se é que foi mesmo à toa.
pt.R: Espero que não tenha sido tudo à toa!

decisions.choice: a note of hope: Paul does not believe it was really in vain
alternatives: a warning: it will prove to be in vain if they turn to the law
decisions.reason: εἴ γε limits what has just been said: "if it really was in vain". Paul is probably holding out hope that it was not, as he does in 5:10. The other reading hears a warning: all they experienced will be wasted if they go on as they are. The two are close, and Paul may mean both.

decisions.choice: I hope it was not all for nothing
alternatives: if indeed it was for nothing
decisions.reason: Readable states the hope that the short phrase implies (meaning note m1). Literal and Balanced keep Paul's open wording.

source.text: ὁ οὖν ἐπιχορηγῶν ὑμῖν τὸ πνεῦμα καὶ ἐνεργῶν δυνάμεις ἐν ὑμῖν ἐξ ἔργων νόμου ἢ ἐξ ἀκοῆς πίστεως;

records.literal_gloss: The [one] therefore supplying to you the Spirit and working miracles among you, by works of law or by hearing of faith?

en.L: So then, the one who supplies the Spirit to you and works miracles among you, [does {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} do it] by works of [the] law, or by [the] hearing of faith?
en.B: So then, does God give you the Spirit and work miracles among you because of works of the law, or because of faith in what you heard?
en.R: God gives you the Spirit and does miracles among you. Does {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} do this because you do what the law commands? Or is it because you heard the message and put your faith in it?

es.L: Así pues, el que {{plural_you:les|os}} suministra el Espíritu y obra milagros entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, ¿[lo hace {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}] por [las] obras de [la] ley, o por [el] oír de [la] fe?
es.B: Entonces, cuando Dios {{plural_you:les|os}} da generosamente el Espíritu y hace milagros entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, ¿lo hace por las obras de la ley, o por la fe en lo que {{plural_you:oyeron|oísteis}}?
es.R: Dios {{plural_you:les|os}} da el Espíritu y hace milagros entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. ¿Lo hace {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} porque {{plural_you:hacen|hacéis}} lo que la ley manda? ¿O es porque {{plural_you:oyeron|oísteis}} el mensaje y {{plural_you:pusieron|pusisteis}} {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} fe en él?

sw.L: Basi, yule anayewapa Roho kwa ukarimu na kutenda miujiza kati yenu, [je, anafanya hivyo] kwa matendo ya sheria, au kwa kusikia kwa imani?
sw.B: Basi, je, Mungu anawapa Roho kwa ukarimu na kutenda miujiza kati yenu kwa sababu ya matendo ya sheria, au kwa sababu mliamini kile mlichosikia?
sw.R: Mungu anawapa Roho, na anatenda miujiza kati yenu. Je, anafanya hivyo kwa sababu mnafanya yale ambayo sheria inaamuru? Au ni kwa sababu mlisikia ujumbe, mkauamini?

fr.L: Celui donc qui vous accorde l’Esprit et qui opère des miracles parmi vous, [le fait-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}}] par les œuvres de la Loi, ou par l’écoute de la foi ?
fr.B: Alors, quand Dieu vous donne l’Esprit et fait des miracles parmi vous, est-ce à cause des œuvres de la Loi, ou à cause de la foi en ce que vous avez entendu ?
fr.R: Dieu vous donne l’Esprit et fait des miracles parmi vous. Le fait-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} parce que vous faites ce que la Loi ordonne ? Ou bien parce que vous avez entendu le message et que vous y avez cru ?

ko.L: 그러면 여러분에게 성령을 주시고 여러분 가운데서 기적들을 행하시는 분께서 [그렇게 하시는 것은] 율법의 행위들로입니까, 아니면 믿음의 들음으로입니까?
ko.B: 그러면 하나님께서 여러분에게 성령을 주시고 여러분 가운데서 기적을 행하시는 것은, 여러분이 율법의 행위를 했기 때문입니까, 아니면 들은 말씀을 믿었기 때문입니까?
ko.R: 하나님께서는 여러분에게 성령을 주시고 여러분 가운데서 기적을 일으키십니다. 그분이 그렇게 하시는 것은 여러분이 율법이 명령하는 것을 행하기 때문입니까? 아니면 여러분이 기쁜 소식을 듣고 그것을 믿었기 때문입니까?

vi.L: Vậy Đấng ban Thánh Linh cho anh chị em và làm các phép lạ giữa anh chị em, [{{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} làm điều đó] bởi những việc làm của luật pháp, hay bởi sự nghe với đức tin?
vi.B: Vậy, có phải Đức Chúa Trời ban Thánh Linh cho anh chị em và làm các phép lạ giữa anh chị em là nhờ những việc luật pháp đòi hỏi, hay nhờ anh chị em tin vào điều mình đã nghe?
vi.R: Đức Chúa Trời ban Thánh Linh cho anh chị em và làm các phép lạ giữa anh chị em. Có phải {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} làm điều đó vì anh chị em làm theo những gì luật pháp truyền dạy không? Hay là vì anh chị em đã nghe sứ điệp và đặt đức tin nơi sứ điệp ấy?

pt.L: Então, aquele que lhes dá o Espírito e opera milagres entre vocês, [faz isso] por obras da Lei, ou pelo ouvir da fé?
pt.B: Então, Deus dá o Espírito a vocês e faz milagres entre vocês por causa das obras da Lei, ou por causa da fé naquilo que vocês ouviram?
pt.R: Deus dá o Espírito a vocês e faz milagres entre vocês. Será que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} faz isso porque vocês fazem o que a Lei manda? Ou é porque vocês ouviram a mensagem e puseram a sua fé nela?

am.L: እንግዲህ መንፈስን የሚሰጣችሁና በመካከላችሁ ተአምራትን የሚሠራው [ይህን የሚያደርገው] ከሕግ ሥራ ነውን ወይስ ከእምነት መስማት?
am.B: እንግዲህ እግዚአብሔር መንፈስን አብዝቶ የሚሰጣችሁና በመካከላችሁ ተአምራትን የሚሠራው በሕግ ሥራ ምክንያት ነው ወይስ የሰማችሁትን በማመናችሁ ምክንያት?
am.R: እግዚአብሔር መንፈስን ይሰጣችኋል፤ በመካከላችሁም ተአምራትን ያደርጋል። ይህን የሚያደርገው ሕጉ የሚለውን ስለምታደርጉ ነው? ወይስ መልእክቱን ሰምታችሁ ስላመናችሁበት ነው?

decisions.choice: the one who supplies the Spirit: God
alternatives: the apostle or another human teacher
decisions.reason: Only God gives the Spirit and works miracles. The present participles say that he goes on doing so among the Galatians; it is not only a past event.

decisions.choice: supplies: gives generously
decisions.reason: ἐπιχορηγέω was used of providing fully for a need. God's giving of the Spirit is generous and continuing.

decisions.choice: miracles among you
decisions.reason: δύναμις in the plural means acts of power, miracles. ἐν ὑμῖν can mean "among you" or "within you"; Paul is appealing to things they had all seen happen in their churches.

decisions.choice: the same choice as in verse 2: works of the law or hearing with faith
decisions.reason: Paul repeats the question of verse 2 word for word, now about what God is still doing among them. The phrase "hearing of faith" is read the same way as there.

decisions.choice: God
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name God, who is meant (meaning note m1).

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}
decisions.reason: A pronoun for God follows the reader's setting.

decisions.choice: works of [the] law (L); works of the law (B); do what the law commands (R)
decisions.reason: As in verse 2.

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun span
alternatives: a span where the English has one
decisions.reason: As in Romans, Swahili marks a pronoun for God inside the verb ("anafanya"), and a prefix cannot take a capital, so the setting applies only to free pronouns and possessives. This sentence has none, so it has no span where the English has "he".

decisions.choice: "phép lạ"
decisions.reason: The Greek word is "powers", mighty works (m3). The Vietnamese John keeps "dấu lạ" for signs; for works of power the plain "phép lạ" is used, as the English says "miracles".

decisions.choice: [faz isso]
decisions.reason: Portuguese, which drops the subject pronoun, needs only the verb in the bracket, so the deity_pronoun span the English Literal has for "he" has no word to sit on here; Readable keeps the pronoun and its span.

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun spans in Amharic
alternatives: capitalised pronouns, as the English alternative has them
decisions.reason: The Ethiopic script has no capital letters, so the setting for capitalised pronouns has nothing to change; pronouns for God and for Christ are written plainly through the letter.

source.text: καθὼς Ἀβραὰμ ἐπίστευσεν τῷ θεῷ, καὶ ἐλογίσθη αὐτῷ εἰς δικαιοσύνην.

records.literal_gloss: Just as Abraham believed the God, and it was reckoned to him as righteousness.

en.L: Just as Abraham believed God, and it was reckoned to him as righteousness.
en.B: So it was with Abraham: he believed God, and it was counted to him as righteousness.
en.R: It was the same with Abraham. He believed God, and because he believed, God accepted him as righteous.

es.L: Así como Abraham creyó a Dios, y le fue acreditado como justicia.
es.B: Así sucedió con Abraham: creyó a Dios, y eso se le acreditó como justicia.
es.R: Lo mismo pasó con Abraham. Él creyó a Dios, y porque creyó, Dios lo aceptó como justo.

sw.L: Kama vile Ibrahimu alivyomwamini Mungu, na [imani hiyo] ikahesabiwa kwake kuwa haki.
sw.B: Ndivyo ilivyokuwa kwa Ibrahimu: alimwamini Mungu, na imani yake ikahesabiwa kwake kuwa haki.
sw.R: Ilikuwa vivyo hivyo kwa Ibrahimu. Alimwamini Mungu, na kwa sababu aliamini, Mungu alimkubali kuwa mwenye haki.

fr.L: De même Abraham crut Dieu, et cela lui fut porté en compte comme justice.
fr.B: Il en va de même pour Abraham : il crut Dieu, et cela lui fut compté comme justice.
fr.R: C’était pareil pour Abraham. Il a cru Dieu, et parce qu’il a cru, Dieu l’a accepté comme juste.

ko.L: 이는 아브라함이 하나님을 믿었더니, 그것이 그에게 의로 여겨진 것과 같습니다.
ko.B: 아브라함도 그러했습니다. 그가 하나님을 믿었더니, 그것이 그에게 의로 여겨졌습니다.
ko.R: 아브라함의 경우도 똑같았습니다. 아브라함은 하나님을 믿었습니다. 그가 믿었기 때문에, 하나님께서는 그를 의롭다고 여겨 주셨습니다.

vi.L: Cũng như Áp-ra-ham đã tin Đức Chúa Trời, và điều đó được kể cho ông là sự công chính.
vi.B: Áp-ra-ham cũng vậy: ông đã tin Đức Chúa Trời, và điều đó được kể cho ông là sự công chính.
vi.R: Áp-ra-ham cũng như vậy. Ông đã tin Đức Chúa Trời, và vì ông tin nên Đức Chúa Trời đã chấp nhận ông là người công chính.

pt.L: Assim como Abraão creu em Deus, e isso lhe foi contado como justiça.
pt.B: Assim aconteceu com Abraão: ele creu em Deus, e isso lhe foi contado como justiça.
pt.R: Foi assim também com Abraão. Ele acreditou em Deus, e por causa disso Deus o aceitou como justo.

am.L: አብርሃም እግዚአብሔርን እንዳመነ፣ [ይህም] ጽድቅ ሆኖ እንደ ተቆጠረለት [ነው]።
am.B: አብርሃምም እንዲሁ ነበር፤ እግዚአብሔርን አመነ፤ ይህም ጽድቅ ሆኖ ተቆጠረለት።
am.R: አብርሃምም እንደዚሁ ነበር። እግዚአብሔርን አመነ፤ ስላመነም እግዚአብሔር ጻድቅ አድርጎ ተቀበለው።

decisions.choice: a quotation of Genesis 15:6
alternatives: a general summary of Abraham's life
decisions.reason: Paul quotes Genesis 15:6 in the words of its Greek translation, without an introductory formula. God had promised Abraham offspring as many as the stars, and Abraham believed him. Paul uses the same verse in Romans 4:3.

decisions.choice: just as: the Galatians' experience matches Abraham's
alternatives: a new argument, unconnected with verses 2-5
decisions.reason: καθώς ties Abraham to what Paul has just said: the Galatians received the Spirit by believing, just as Abraham was accepted by believing. The Jewish teachers in Galatia probably pointed to Abraham, who was circumcised (Genesis 17); Paul points to Genesis 15, which comes before it.

decisions.choice: reckoned: counted, entered to his account
decisions.reason: λογίζομαι is a word from bookkeeping: something is entered to a person's account. God counted Abraham's believing as righteousness. The "it" is his believing.

decisions.choice: righteousness: a right standing with God
decisions.reason: Righteousness here is the standing of one who is in the right before God, as the word "justify" in verses 8 and 11 shows.

decisions.choice: reckoned (L); counted (B)
decisions.reason: Both keep the picture of an entry in an account.

decisions.choice: because he believed, God accepted him as righteous
alternatives: it was counted to him as righteousness
decisions.reason: Readable says who did the counting and what "it" refers to (meaning note m3). It keeps the key word in the form "righteous".

decisions.choice: acreditar
decisions.reason: The meaning decision describes a word from bookkeeping: something entered to a person's account. "Acreditar" is the Spanish bookkeeping word for that, and still common; "imputar", the older wording, now usually means to charge someone with a crime.

decisions.choice: [imani hiyo] ikahesabiwa kwake kuwa haki (L); imani yake ikahesabiwa (B)
decisions.reason: Swahili needs a subject for "was reckoned", and the meaning decision says the "it" is Abraham's believing, so Literal supplies "[imani hiyo]" and Balanced says "imani yake". "Akahesabiwa haki" would turn the sentence into the settled verb for "justify". Keeping "kuhesabiwa ... kuwa haki" still lets the reader see that the two belong together, as Paul's argument in verses 6-8 does.

decisions.choice: passé simple for the words of Genesis 15:6 (L, B: "crut", "fut compté"); passé composé (R)
decisions.reason: Paul quotes a sentence of the Genesis narrative, and the French style guide puts narrative in the passé simple at Literal and Balanced, as Hebrews does for Genesis. Paul's own argument around it stays in the present and the passé composé; Readable uses the passé composé throughout.

decisions.choice: porté en compte (L); compté (B)
decisions.reason: The verb is a bookkeeping word, an entry made to someone's account (m3). "Porter en compte" keeps the picture at Literal; "imputer" is church language.

decisions.choice: "의로 여겨졌습니다" (L, B); "의롭다고 여겨 주셨습니다" (R)
decisions.reason: As in Romans 4:3: the verb is a bookkeeping word, to put to someone's account (the meaning decision), and "여기다" (count as) is plain enough for every level; "인정하다" is kept for the verdict word "의롭다고 인정하다", so the two verbs stay apart. "의" stays the key term.

decisions.choice: "được kể ... là sự công chính" (L, B)
decisions.reason: The bookkeeping verb of Genesis 15:6 (m3), which the Vietnamese Romans keeps as "kể" (4:3) wherever it appears; Readable says what it means, as the English Readable does. "Ông" is the respectful pronoun for Abraham, as in the Vietnamese Romans.

decisions.choice: lhe foi contado como justiça
decisions.reason: For the whole book, as in Romans 4: "contar como" keeps the picture of an entry in an account (m3) in everyday Portuguese; "imputar" is legal jargon and "creditar" banking language. Readable says who counted and what "it" was, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: ጽድቅ ሆኖ ተቆጠረለት (it was counted to him as righteousness)
decisions.reason: The verb is a word of accounts: entered to his credit (meaning decision m3). "ተቆጠረለት" (was counted to him) keeps that picture, and "ጽድቅ" stays the key term for righteousness.

source.text: Γινώσκετε ἄρα ὅτι οἱ ἐκ πίστεως, οὗτοι υἱοί εἰσιν Ἀβραάμ.

records.literal_gloss: Know then that those of faith, these sons are of Abraham.

en.L: Know, then, that those [who are] of faith, these are {{gender:children|sons}} of Abraham.
en.B: You can see, then, that the people of faith are the ones who are Abraham's {{gender:children|sons}}.
en.R: So understand this: the people who live by faith are Abraham's real {{gender:children|sons}}.

es.L: {{plural_you:Sepan|Sabed}}, pues, que los [que son] de fe, estos son hijos de Abraham.
es.B: {{plural_you:Pueden|Podéis}} ver, entonces, que los que se apoyan en la fe son los hijos de Abraham.
es.R: Así que {{plural_you:entiendan|entended}} esto: los que viven por la fe son los verdaderos hijos de Abraham.

sw.L: Jueni basi kwamba wale [walio] wa imani, hao ni wana wa Ibrahimu.
sw.B: Basi mnaweza kuona kwamba watu wa imani ndio wana wa Ibrahimu.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo elewani jambo hili: watu wanaoishi kwa imani ndio wana halisi wa Ibrahimu.

fr.L: Sachez donc que ceux qui [relèvent] de la foi, ceux-là sont {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Abraham.
fr.B: Vous le voyez donc : ce sont les gens de foi qui sont les {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Abraham.
fr.R: Alors comprenez bien ceci : les gens qui vivent par la foi sont les vrais {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Abraham.

ko.L: 그러므로 믿음으로 말미암은 사람들, 바로 이들이 아브라함의 {{gender:자녀|아들}}들임을 아십시오.
ko.B: 그러니 믿음의 사람들이야말로 아브라함의 {{gender:자녀|아들}}들이라는 것을 알 수 있습니다.
ko.R: 그러므로 이것을 깨달으십시오. 믿음으로 사는 사람들이 아브라함의 진짜 {{gender:자녀|아들}}들입니다.

vi.L: Vậy, hãy biết rằng những người [sống] bởi đức tin, chính họ là con cái của Áp-ra-ham.
vi.B: Vậy anh chị em có thể thấy rằng những người có đức tin mới là con cái của Áp-ra-ham.
vi.R: Vậy hãy hiểu điều này: những người sống bởi đức tin mới là con cái thật của Áp-ra-ham.

pt.L: Saibam, portanto, que os que [são] da fé, esses são filhos de Abraão.
pt.B: Vocês podem ver, então, que as pessoas de fé é que são os filhos de Abraão.
pt.R: Por isso entendam isto: as pessoas que vivem pela fé é que são os verdadeiros filhos de Abraão.

am.L: እንግዲያስ ከእምነት የሆኑት፣ እነዚህ የአብርሃም ልጆች እንደ ሆኑ እወቁ።
am.B: እንግዲህ የአብርሃም ልጆች የእምነት ሰዎች መሆናቸውን ታያላችሁ።
am.R: ስለዚህ ይህን አስተውሉ፤ በእምነት የሚኖሩ ሰዎች እውነተኛ የአብርሃም ልጆች ናቸው።

decisions.choice: an instruction: know, understand
decisions.reason: Γινώσκετε can be a command or a statement of what they know. Either way Paul draws a conclusion from Genesis 15:6, as ἄρα ("then") shows.

decisions.choice: those of faith: people whose standing with God comes from faith
alternatives: people who are loyal or faithful
decisions.reason: The phrase describes people by where their life with God comes from. Paul sets them against "those who are of works of the law" in verse 10.

decisions.choice: sons of Abraham: his true descendants and heirs
decisions.reason: In the Scriptures being someone's υἱός means belonging to his family, sharing his character and inheriting what is his. The word gives the status of a son and heir, which Paul applies to men and women alike (3:28-29). Those who believe, as Abraham did, are his family, whether or not they are descended from him.

decisions.choice: {{gender:children|sons}}
decisions.reason: The word means men and women here (meaning note m3), so it follows the gender setting.

decisions.choice: live by faith; real
decisions.reason: Readable explains the short phrase "those of faith" and adds "real" to bring out the contrast with physical descent (meaning note m3).

decisions.choice: hijos, no setting
decisions.reason: As in Romans, Spanish "hijos" already covers sons and daughters, so the English gender setting has nothing to change, and "hijos e hijas" would add words the Greek does not have. "Hijos" also keeps the status of heir the meaning decision describes.

decisions.choice: los que se apoyan en la fe
decisions.reason: "Los de la fe" is not natural Spanish prose. "Los que se apoyan en la fe" (those who rely on faith) says what the meaning decision describes, and verse 10 uses the same verb for those who rely on works of the law, so the contrast stays visible. Verse 9 repeats it.

decisions.choice: wana, no setting
decisions.reason: "Wana" means children, sons and daughters alike, and is the word for heirs, so the English gender setting has nothing to change in Swahili; adding "wa kiume" (male) would change the meaning.

decisions.choice: {{gender:enfants|fils}} d'Abraham (for the whole letter, wherever the English has the span)
decisions.reason: As in Hebrews 2:10: the word gives the standing of a son and heir to men and women alike (m3), so "enfants" is the default and the traditional "fils" the alternative. The words around it are chosen to read correctly with both ("les enfants" / "les fils").

decisions.choice: ceux qui [relèvent] de la foi (L); the same in 3:9, and "ceux qui [relèvent] des œuvres de la Loi" in 3:10
alternatives: ceux qui sont de la foi
decisions.reason: French cannot say "ceux qui sont de la foi" for people whose standing comes from faith (m2). Literal supplies a verb in brackets that keeps the parallel with 3:10.

decisions.choice: {{gender:자녀|아들}}들 at every level
decisions.reason: The Greek says "sons", meaning Abraham's true descendants and heirs, women and men (the meaning decision). Korean has two ways to say it, "자녀" (children) and the traditional "아들", so the gender setting applies, as it does in the English; the plural "들" stays outside the span.

decisions.choice: "con cái của Áp-ra-ham", with no gender span
decisions.reason: "Con cái" already includes sons and daughters, as the Vietnamese Colossians notes (3:6), so there is no second wording for the setting to offer; "con trai" would narrow the sense of true descendants and heirs (m3). The same holds in 3:26 and 4:6-7.

decisions.choice: filhos, with no gender setting
decisions.reason: The English puts "children|sons" under the gender setting. Portuguese "filhos" already includes sons and daughters while keeping the standing of a son and heir that m3 describes, so it needs no setting, as in Romans 8:14.

decisions.choice: የአብርሃም ልጆች (Abraham's children), with no gender span, here and through chapters 3-4
decisions.reason: The English offers "children" and "sons". "ልጆች" already covers sons and daughters, and "ወንዶች ልጆች" would stress maleness, which the phrase does not do here (meaning decision m3), so Amharic needs no span, as in Romans 8:14.

source.text: προϊδοῦσα δὲ ἡ γραφὴ ὅτι ἐκ πίστεως δικαιοῖ τὰ ἔθνη ὁ θεὸς προευηγγελίσατο τῷ Ἀβραὰμ ὅτι Ἐνευλογηθήσονται ἐν σοὶ πάντα τὰ ἔθνη.

records.literal_gloss: Having foreseen and the Scripture that by faith justifies the Gentiles the God, proclaimed the gospel beforehand to the Abraham: Will be blessed in you all the nations.

en.L: And the Scripture, foreseeing that God justifies the Gentiles by faith, proclaimed the gospel beforehand to Abraham: "All the nations will be blessed in you."
en.B: Scripture saw in advance that God would justify the Gentiles by faith, and so it announced the gospel ahead of time to Abraham: "In you all the nations will be blessed."
en.R: Long before, Scripture looked ahead and saw that God would put the Gentiles right with {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} by faith. So it told Abraham the good news ahead of time: "Because of you, all the nations will be blessed."

es.L: Y la Escritura, previendo que Dios justifica a los gentiles por [la] fe, anunció de antemano el evangelio a Abraham: «En ti serán benditas todas las naciones».
es.B: La Escritura vio de antemano que Dios justificaría a los gentiles por la fe, y por eso anunció con anticipación el evangelio a Abraham: «En ti serán bendecidas todas las naciones».
es.R: Mucho tiempo antes, la Escritura miró hacia adelante y vio que Dios declararía justos a los gentiles por medio de la fe. Por eso le dio a Abraham la buena noticia antes de tiempo: «Gracias a ti, todas las naciones serán bendecidas».

sw.L: Na Maandiko, yakitangulia kuona kwamba Mungu huwahesabia haki watu wa mataifa kwa imani, yalimtangazia Ibrahimu Injili mapema: "Mataifa yote yatabarikiwa ndani yako."
sw.B: Maandiko yaliona mapema kwamba Mungu angewahesabia haki watu wa mataifa kwa imani, kwa hiyo yakamtangazia Ibrahimu Injili kabla ya wakati wake: "Ndani yako mataifa yote yatabarikiwa."
sw.R: Zamani sana, Maandiko yalitazama mbele na kuona kwamba Mungu angewahesabia haki watu wa mataifa kwa imani. Kwa hiyo yalimpa Ibrahimu Habari Njema kabla ya wakati wake: "Kwa sababu yako, mataifa yote yatabarikiwa."

fr.L: Et l’Écriture, prévoyant que Dieu justifie les nations par la foi, a annoncé d’avance l’Évangile à Abraham : « En toi seront bénies toutes les nations. »
fr.B: L’Écriture a vu d’avance que Dieu justifierait les nations par la foi, et c’est pourquoi elle a annoncé d’avance l’Évangile à Abraham : « En toi toutes les nations seront bénies. »
fr.R: Longtemps à l’avance, l’Écriture a regardé vers l’avenir et a vu que Dieu déclarerait justes devant {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, par la foi, les gens qui ne sont pas juifs. Elle a donc annoncé d’avance la bonne nouvelle à Abraham : « Grâce à toi, toutes les nations seront bénies. »

ko.L: 또 성경은 하나님께서 이방 사람들을 믿음으로 의롭다고 인정하실 것을 미리 보고, 아브라함에게 "모든 민족이 너 안에서 복을 받을 것이다" 하고 복음을 미리 전하였습니다.
ko.B: 성경은 하나님께서 이방 사람들을 믿음으로 의롭다고 인정하실 것을 미리 내다보고, 아브라함에게 "모든 민족이 너로 말미암아 복을 받을 것이다" 하는 복음을 미리 알려 주었습니다.
ko.R: 아주 오래전에 성경은 앞일을 내다보았습니다. 하나님께서 유대인이 아닌 사람들도 믿음으로 의롭다고 인정해 주실 것을 본 것입니다. 그래서 성경은 아브라함에게 이 기쁜 소식을 미리 전해 주었습니다. "너 때문에 모든 민족이 복을 받을 것이다."

vi.L: Và Kinh Thánh, thấy trước rằng Đức Chúa Trời xưng công chính các dân ngoại bởi đức tin, đã rao Tin Lành trước cho Áp-ra-ham: "Mọi dân tộc sẽ được phước trong con."
vi.B: Kinh Thánh đã thấy trước rằng Đức Chúa Trời sẽ xưng công chính các dân ngoại bởi đức tin, nên đã báo trước Tin Lành cho Áp-ra-ham: "Trong con, mọi dân tộc sẽ được phước."
vi.R: Từ rất lâu trước, Kinh Thánh đã nhìn trước và thấy rằng Đức Chúa Trời sẽ công nhận các dân ngoại là công chính nhờ đức tin. Vì vậy Kinh Thánh đã báo trước Tin Lành cho Áp-ra-ham: "Nhờ con, mọi dân tộc sẽ được phước."

pt.L: E a Escritura, prevendo que Deus justifica as nações pela fé, anunciou de antemão o evangelho a Abraão: "Em ti serão abençoadas todas as nações."
pt.B: A Escritura viu de antemão que Deus declararia justos os não judeus pela fé, e por isso anunciou antecipadamente o evangelho a Abraão: "Em ti todas as nações serão abençoadas."
pt.R: Muito tempo antes, a Escritura olhou para o futuro e viu que Deus aceitaria os não judeus como justos diante de {{deity_pronoun:si|Si}}, pela fé. Por isso ela anunciou antecipadamente as boas-novas a Abraão: "Por causa de ti, todas as nações serão abençoadas."

am.L: መጽሐፍም እግዚአብሔር አሕዛብን በእምነት እንደሚያጸድቅ አስቀድሞ አይቶ፣ ለአብርሃም አስቀድሞ ወንጌልን እንዲህ ሲል ሰበከ፦ «አሕዛብ ሁሉ በአንተ ይባረካሉ።»
am.B: መጽሐፍ እግዚአብሔር አሕዛብን በእምነት እንደሚያጸድቅ አስቀድሞ አየ፤ ስለዚህ ለአብርሃም አስቀድሞ ወንጌልን እንዲህ ብሎ አበሰረ፦ «አሕዛብ ሁሉ በአንተ ይባረካሉ።»
am.R: ከብዙ ዘመን በፊት መጽሐፍ ወደ ፊት ተመልክቶ እግዚአብሔር አይሁድ ያልሆኑትን ሕዝቦች በእምነት ከራሱ ጋር ትክክለኛ ግንኙነት እንዲኖራቸው እንደሚያደርግ አየ። ስለዚህ የምሥራቹን አስቀድሞ ለአብርሃም እንዲህ ብሎ ነገረው፦ «በአንተ ምክንያት ሕዝቦች ሁሉ ይባረካሉ።»

decisions.choice: Scripture foresaw: God speaking in Scripture
decisions.reason: Paul speaks of Scripture as if it could see ahead and preach. He means God, who spoke the words recorded in it and knew what he would do (compare 3:22 and Romans 9:17).

decisions.choice: God declares a person to be in the right before him: acquitted and accepted
alternatives: a person proves to be good
decisions.reason: δικαιόω is a word from the law court: the judge declares someone to be in the right. Here God is the judge, and the person he justifies is accepted by him and stands in the right before him (2:16). It is a verdict God gives, not a reward for good conduct.

decisions.choice: a quotation of God's promise in Genesis 12:3 and 18:18
alternatives: a general blessing on Abraham alone
decisions.reason: The words come from God's promise to Abraham in Genesis 12:3 ("in you all the families of the earth will be blessed") and 18:18 ("all the nations of the earth"). Paul calls that promise the gospel announced in advance: already then God meant to bless the Gentiles.

decisions.choice: nations and Gentiles: the same word
decisions.reason: ἔθνος means both "nations" and "Gentiles", the peoples other than Israel. Paul's point depends on it: the nations promised a blessing in Genesis are the Gentiles God now justifies by faith.

decisions.choice: in you: through Abraham, and as people joined to him
decisions.reason: The nations are blessed because of Abraham and by sharing in the blessing given to him; verse 9 says they are blessed "with" him. The promise comes to them in Christ (verse 14).

decisions.choice: justifies / would justify (L, B); put right with himself (R)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the legal word "justify". Readable says what it means: God puts a person right with him (meaning note m2).

decisions.choice: Gentiles ... nations
decisions.reason: English needs two words for the one Greek word; meaning note m4 shows they are the same.

decisions.choice: proclaimed the gospel beforehand (L); announced the gospel ahead of time (B); told the good news ahead of time (R)
decisions.reason: The verb contains the word for the gospel. Literal and Balanced say "gospel"; Readable says "good news", as it does for the noun.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}
decisions.reason: A pronoun for God follows the reader's setting.

decisions.choice: because of you
decisions.reason: Readable gives the plain sense of "in you" (meaning note m5).

decisions.choice: justificar (L, B); declarar justo (R)
alternatives: poner en una relación correcta con Dios (R)
decisions.reason: As settled in Romans, Literal and Balanced keep "justificar", and Readable says "declarar justo", which keeps the verdict of the law court the meaning decision describes. So the Spanish Readable has no pronoun for God where the English says "put ... right with himself".

decisions.choice: kuwahesabia haki
decisions.reason: As settled in Romans, "kuhesabiwa haki" is kept at every level, here in the active form with God as subject. Readable needs no further explanation, since the phrase already says that God counts people righteous.

decisions.choice: watu wa mataifa ... mataifa yote
decisions.reason: The meaning decision says Paul's point rests on one Greek word for "Gentiles" and "nations". Swahili keeps the same word, "mataifa", in both places, so the reader can see the link without a note.

decisions.choice: les nations ... toutes les nations (L, B)
decisions.reason: French can use one word where English needs "Gentiles" and "nations", so Literal and Balanced show what Paul's argument rests on (m4): the nations blessed in Genesis are the nations God justifies by faith. Readable explains the first.

decisions.choice: "이방 사람들" (L, B) / "유대인이 아닌 사람들" (R) and "모든 민족" for the same Greek word
alternatives: the same Korean word for both
decisions.reason: The Greek uses one word for "the Gentiles" and "the nations" (the meaning decision). Korean has no single word for both senses; "모든 민족" is the natural word in the promise to Abraham, and Paul's point, that the promise reaches the non-Jewish peoples, is plain from the two words side by side.

decisions.choice: God's words to Abraham in 해라체 with "너"
decisions.reason: The quotation gives God's promise, spoken to Abraham, and God speaks in 해라체 in the Korean of the Old Testament (docs/korean-style.md section 7a).

decisions.choice: "các dân ngoại" for the Gentiles, "mọi dân tộc" in the quotation
decisions.reason: One Greek word stands behind both (m4). Paul's point is that the promise to all the nations reaches the Gentiles, so Vietnamese keeps the general word in God's promise, as the Vietnamese Romans does (1:5), and "dân ngoại" in Paul's own words.

decisions.choice: "con" for Abraham in God's words
decisions.reason: God speaks to Abraham as a father to one he cares for, as in the Vietnamese Romans (4:17); "ngươi" is archaic.

decisions.choice: as nações ... as nações (L); os não judeus ... as nações (B, R)
decisions.reason: Portuguese, like English, needs two words for the one Greek word at Balanced and Readable (m4); Literal keeps "as nações" both times, so the reader sees that the promise and its fulfilment speak of the same peoples.

decisions.choice: ti (God speaking to Abraham)
decisions.reason: God's promise is quoted as he spoke it to Abraham, with "tu" at every level, as God addresses people in the Old Testament (style section 4).

decisions.choice: አሕዛብ (Gentiles, nations) for both words
decisions.reason: Paul's argument rests on one Greek word meaning both the Gentiles and the nations of the promise (meaning decision m4). "አሕዛብ" also means both, so Literal and Balanced use it twice; Readable, which says "people who are not Jews" for the Gentiles, says "ሕዝቦች ሁሉ" in the promise.

source.text: ὥστε οἱ ἐκ πίστεως εὐλογοῦνται σὺν τῷ πιστῷ Ἀβραάμ.

records.literal_gloss: So then those of faith are blessed with the believing Abraham.

en.L: So then those [who are] of faith are blessed along with Abraham, the believer.
en.B: So the people of faith share in the blessing together with Abraham, who believed.
en.R: So everyone who lives by faith is blessed together with Abraham, who believed God.

es.L: De modo que los [que son] de fe son bendecidos junto con Abraham, el creyente.
es.B: Así que los que se apoyan en la fe comparten la bendición junto con Abraham, que creyó.
es.R: Así que todos los que viven por la fe son bendecidos junto con Abraham, que creyó a Dios.

sw.L: Hivyo wale [walio] wa imani wanabarikiwa pamoja na Ibrahimu, yule mwamini.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo watu wa imani wanashiriki baraka pamoja na Ibrahimu, mtu aliyeamini.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo kila mtu anayeishi kwa imani anabarikiwa pamoja na Ibrahimu, aliyemwamini Mungu.

fr.L: De sorte que ceux qui [relèvent] de la foi sont bénis avec Abraham le croyant.
fr.B: Ainsi, les gens de foi ont part à la bénédiction avec Abraham, qui a cru.
fr.R: Ainsi, tous ceux qui vivent par la foi sont bénis avec Abraham, qui a cru Dieu.

ko.L: 그러므로 믿음으로 말미암은 사람들은 믿은 [사람] 아브라함과 함께 복을 받습니다.
ko.B: 그러므로 믿음의 사람들은 믿은 사람 아브라함과 함께 복을 받습니다.
ko.R: 그러므로 믿음으로 사는 사람은 누구나 하나님을 믿은 아브라함과 함께 복을 받습니다.

vi.L: Vậy, những người [sống] bởi đức tin được phước cùng với Áp-ra-ham, người có lòng tin.
vi.B: Vậy những người có đức tin cùng được hưởng phước với Áp-ra-ham, người đã tin.
vi.R: Vì vậy, tất cả những ai sống bởi đức tin đều được phước cùng với Áp-ra-ham, là người đã tin Đức Chúa Trời.

pt.L: De modo que os que [são] da fé são abençoados com Abraão, o que creu.
pt.B: Assim, as pessoas de fé participam da bênção junto com Abraão, que creu.
pt.R: Por isso todas as pessoas que vivem pela fé são abençoadas junto com Abraão, que acreditou em Deus.

am.L: ስለዚህ ከእምነት የሆኑት ካመነው ከአብርሃም ጋር ይባረካሉ።
am.B: ስለዚህ የእምነት ሰዎች ካመነው ከአብርሃም ጋር በበረከቱ ይካፈላሉ።
am.R: ስለዚህ በእምነት የሚኖር ሁሉ እግዚአብሔርን ካመነው ከአብርሃም ጋር አብሮ ይባረካል።

decisions.choice: believing: Abraham who trusted God
decisions.reason: πιστός can mean faithful or believing. Coming straight after "Abraham believed God" (verse 6), it points to his believing.

decisions.choice: with Abraham: sharing the one blessing given to him
alternatives: blessed in the same way as Abraham
decisions.reason: σύν means together with. Believers do not receive a blessing like his; they share the blessing God promised him (verse 8).

decisions.choice: lives by faith; believed God
decisions.reason: Readable explains the short phrases, as in verse 7.

source.text: Ὅσοι γὰρ ἐξ ἔργων νόμου εἰσὶν ὑπὸ κατάραν εἰσίν, γέγραπται γὰρ ὅτι Ἐπικατάρατος πᾶς ὃς οὐκ ἐμμένει πᾶσιν τοῖς γεγραμμένοις ἐν τῷ βιβλίῳ τοῦ νόμου τοῦ ποιῆσαι αὐτά.

records.literal_gloss: As many as for of works of law are, under curse are; it has been written for: Cursed everyone who not remains in all the things having been written in the book of the law to do them.

en.L: For as many as are of works of [the] law are under a curse, for it is written, "Cursed [is] everyone who does not remain in all the things written in the book of the law, to do them."
en.B: For everyone whose standing rests on works of the law is under a curse. Scripture says, "A curse is on everyone who does not hold fast to everything written in the book of the law and do it."
en.R: People who depend on doing what the law commands are under a curse. Scripture says, "Everyone who does not keep on doing all that is written in the book of the law is under a curse."

es.L: Porque todos los que son de [las] obras de [la] ley están bajo maldición, pues está escrito: «Maldito [es] todo el que no permanece en todas las cosas escritas en el libro de la ley, para hacerlas».
es.B: Porque todos los que se apoyan en las obras de la ley para estar bien con Dios están bajo maldición. La Escritura dice: «Maldito sea todo el que no persevere en cumplir todo lo que está escrito en el libro de la ley».
es.R: Los que dependen de hacer lo que la ley manda están bajo maldición. La Escritura dice: «Todo el que no sigue haciendo todo lo que está escrito en el libro de la ley está bajo maldición».

sw.L: Kwa maana wote ambao ni wa matendo ya sheria wako chini ya laana; kwa sababu imeandikwa, "[Ni] mlaaniwa kila mtu ambaye haendelei katika mambo yote yaliyoandikwa katika kitabu cha sheria, ili kuyatenda."
sw.B: Kwa maana wote wanaotegemea matendo ya sheria ili wakubaliwe na Mungu wako chini ya laana. Maandiko yanasema, "Laana iko juu ya kila mtu asiyeshikamana na yote yaliyoandikwa katika kitabu cha sheria na kuyatenda."
sw.R: Watu wanaotegemea kufanya yale ambayo sheria inaamuru wako chini ya laana. Maandiko yanasema, "Kila mtu asiyeendelea kufanya yote yaliyoandikwa katika kitabu cha sheria yuko chini ya laana."

fr.L: Car tous ceux qui [relèvent] des œuvres de la Loi sont sous une malédiction, car il est écrit : « Maudit [est] quiconque ne demeure pas dans toutes les choses écrites dans le livre de la Loi, pour les faire. »
fr.B: Car tous ceux qui comptent sur les œuvres de la Loi sont sous une malédiction. L’Écriture dit en effet : « La malédiction est sur quiconque ne s’en tient pas à tout ce qui est écrit dans le livre de la Loi pour le mettre en pratique. »
fr.R: Les gens qui comptent sur ce qu’ils font pour obéir à la Loi sont sous une malédiction. L’Écriture dit : « Quiconque ne continue pas à faire tout ce qui est écrit dans le livre de la Loi est sous la malédiction. »

ko.L: 율법의 행위들에 속한 사람들은 다 저주 아래 있습니다. "율법책에 기록된 모든 것을 계속 지켜 행하지 않는 사람은 누구나 저주를 받는다"라고 기록되어 있기 때문입니다.
ko.B: 율법의 행위에 기대는 사람은 누구나 저주 아래 있습니다. 성경에 "율법책에 기록된 모든 것을 굳게 지켜 행하지 않는 사람은 누구나 저주를 받는다" 하였습니다.
ko.R: 율법이 명령하는 것을 행하는 데 기대는 사람들은 저주 아래 있습니다. 성경은 이렇게 말합니다. "율법책에 기록된 모든 것을 끝까지 행하지 않는 사람은 누구나 저주를 받는다."

vi.L: Vì tất cả những ai [cậy] vào những việc làm của luật pháp đều ở dưới sự nguyền rủa, vì có chép: "Đáng nguyền rủa thay mọi người không cứ ở trong mọi điều đã chép trong sách luật pháp để làm theo."
vi.B: Vì tất cả những ai đặt địa vị mình trên những việc luật pháp đòi hỏi đều ở dưới sự nguyền rủa. Kinh Thánh có chép: "Sự nguyền rủa ở trên mọi người không giữ vững và không làm theo mọi điều đã chép trong sách luật pháp."
vi.R: Những người trông cậy vào việc làm theo những gì luật pháp truyền dạy đều ở dưới sự nguyền rủa. Kinh Thánh chép: "Ai không luôn luôn làm theo mọi điều đã chép trong sách luật pháp thì đều ở dưới sự nguyền rủa."

pt.L: Pois todos os que são de obras da Lei estão debaixo de maldição, pois está escrito: "Maldito [é] todo aquele que não persiste em tudo o que está escrito no livro da Lei, para fazê-lo."
pt.B: Pois todo aquele que se apoia nas obras da Lei está debaixo de maldição. A Escritura diz: "Está debaixo de maldição todo aquele que não se mantém firme em tudo o que está escrito no livro da Lei, para cumpri-lo."
pt.R: As pessoas que dependem de fazer o que a Lei manda estão debaixo de maldição. A Escritura diz: "Todo aquele que não continua fazendo tudo o que está escrito no livro da Lei está debaixo de maldição."

am.L: ከሕግ ሥራ የሆኑ ሁሉ ከእርግማን በታች ናቸውና፤ «በሕግ መጽሐፍ የተጻፈውን ሁሉ ለማድረግ በእርሱ የማይጸና ሁሉ የተረገመ ነው» ተብሎ ተጽፏልና።
am.B: አቋማቸው በሕግ ሥራ ላይ የተመሠረተ ሁሉ ከእርግማን በታች ናቸው። መጽሐፍ እንዲህ ይላል፦ «በሕግ መጽሐፍ የተጻፈውን ሁሉ አጥብቆ የማይይዝና የማያደርግ ሁሉ እርግማን አለበት።»
am.R: ሕጉ የሚለውን በማድረግ ላይ የሚደገፉ ሰዎች ከእርግማን በታች ናቸው። መጽሐፍ እንዲህ ይላል፦ «በሕግ መጽሐፍ የተጻፈውን ሁሉ ማድረግ የማይቀጥል ማንም ከእርግማን በታች ነው።»

decisions.choice: a quotation of Deuteronomy 27:26
decisions.reason: The words are from Deuteronomy 27:26, the last of the curses announced when Israel entered the land, in the form of its Greek translation; "the book of the law" echoes Deuteronomy 28:58 and 29:20.

decisions.choice: a curse: God's judgment on those who break his covenant
decisions.reason: In Deuteronomy the law ends with blessings for obedience and curses for disobedience (Deuteronomy 27-28). The curse is the opposite of the blessing in verse 9.

decisions.choice: relying on the law brings a curse, because no one keeps all of it
alternatives: relying on the law is itself the curse, whether one keeps it or not
decisions.reason: Paul leaves a step unstated. The law curses everyone who does not do all it requires; no one does (2:16, 6:13); so those who look to the law for their standing with God fall under its curse. Others read the verse without that unstated step: the law's way of doing is itself not the way of faith (verse 12). Both readings agree that the law cannot bring the blessing.

decisions.choice: remain in: keep on obeying
decisions.reason: ἐμμένω means to stay with something, here to keep on doing all the law commands.

decisions.choice: of works of [the] law (L); whose standing rests on works of the law (B); depend on doing what the law commands (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what it means to be "of" works of the law: to look to them for one's standing with God.

decisions.choice: Scripture says
decisions.reason: The usual formula for quoting Scripture, put in plain English.

decisions.choice: kitabu cha sheria
decisions.reason: "Torati" is the familiar Swahili name for the books of Moses, but "sheria" is the word Paul's argument turns on in the whole sentence ("matendo ya sheria", "laana ya sheria" in verse 13), so Swahili keeps it here too.

decisions.choice: Maudit [est] quiconque (L); the same form in 3:13
decisions.reason: The Greek states a fact, not a wish, so Literal supplies "est" rather than the wish form "soit". Balanced says "La malédiction est sur" in both quotations, so that the two curses still meet (m3 on 3:13).

decisions.choice: Scripture quoted in the plain written style (해라체: "저주를 받는다")
decisions.reason: Quotations of the law and the prophets keep the plain written style of Scripture in Korean, set apart from the 합쇼체 of the letter, as in Colossians 2:21 and Romans. The archaic endings of the older Bibles are not used.

decisions.choice: "sự nguyền rủa", "đáng nguyền rủa" for the curse through 3:10-13
decisions.reason: The curse is God's judgment on those who break his covenant (m2). "Nguyền rủa" is the word for "accursed" in 1:8-9, so the family stays one; "rủa sả" is older church language.

decisions.choice: "như có chép" (L); "Kinh Thánh có chép" (B); "Kinh Thánh chép" (R) for "it is written" (for the whole letter)
decisions.reason: "Chép" is the verb Vietnamese uses for what stands written in Scripture, as in the Vietnamese Romans (1:17); Balanced and Readable name Scripture, as the English does.

source.text: ὅτι δὲ ἐν νόμῳ οὐδεὶς δικαιοῦται παρὰ τῷ θεῷ δῆλον, ὅτι Ὁ δίκαιος ἐκ πίστεως ζήσεται, ὁ δὲ νόμος οὐκ ἔστιν ἐκ πίστεως, ἀλλ’· Ὁ ποιήσας αὐτὰ ζήσεται ἐν αὐτοῖς.

records.literal_gloss: That and by law no one is justified before the God [is] evident, because: The righteous by faith will live; \v 12 the and law not is of faith, but: The [one] having done them will live by them.

en.L: And that no one is justified before God by [the] law [is] evident, because "The righteous [one] will live by faith." \v 12 But the law is not of faith; rather, "The one who does them will live by them."
en.B: It is plain that no one is justified in God's sight through the law, since "The one who is righteous will live by faith." \v 12 But the law does not rest on faith. Instead, "Whoever does these things will live by them."
en.R: It is clear that no one is put right with God by keeping the law. Scripture says, "Those who are righteous will live by faith." \v 12 But the law is not based on faith. The law says, "The person who does these things will live by doing them."

es.L: Y que por [la] ley nadie es justificado delante de Dios [es] evidente, porque «El justo vivirá por [la] fe». \v 12 Pero la ley no es de fe, sino que «El que las haga vivirá por ellas».
es.B: Es evidente que nadie es justificado ante Dios por la ley, ya que «El que es justo vivirá por la fe». \v 12 Pero la ley no se basa en la fe. Al contrario: «Quien haga estas cosas vivirá por ellas».
es.R: Está claro que Dios no declara justo a nadie porque cumpla la ley. La Escritura dice: «La persona que es justa vivirá por la fe». \v 12 Pero la ley no se basa en la fe. La ley dice: «La persona que hace estas cosas vivirá por hacerlas».

sw.L: Na kwamba kwa sheria hakuna anayehesabiwa haki mbele za Mungu [ni] wazi, kwa sababu "Mwenye haki ataishi kwa imani." \v 12 Lakini sheria si ya imani; bali, "Yule aliyeyatenda ataishi kwa hayo."
sw.B: Kwa njia ya sheria hakuna mtu anayehesabiwa haki machoni pa Mungu; hilo ni wazi, kwa kuwa "Mtu aliye mwenye haki ataishi kwa imani." \v 12 Lakini sheria haijajengwa juu ya imani. Badala yake, "Mtu anayeyatenda mambo haya ataishi kwa hayo."
sw.R: Ni wazi kwamba hakuna mtu anayehesabiwa haki na Mungu kwa kushika sheria. Maandiko yanasema, "Mtu aliye mwenye haki ataishi kwa imani." \v 12 Lakini sheria haitegemei imani. Sheria inasema, "Mtu anayefanya mambo haya ataishi kwa kuyafanya."

fr.L: Et que par la Loi personne ne soit justifié devant Dieu, [c’est] évident, car : « Le juste vivra par la foi. » \v 12 Or la Loi n’est pas de la foi, mais : « Celui qui les aura pratiquées vivra par elles. »
fr.B: Il est clair que personne n’est justifié devant Dieu par la Loi, puisque « celui qui est juste vivra par la foi ». \v 12 Or la Loi ne repose pas sur la foi. Au contraire : « Celui qui met ces choses en pratique vivra par elles. »
fr.R: Il est clair que personne n’est déclaré juste par Dieu parce qu’il obéit à la Loi. L’Écriture dit : « Ceux qui sont justes vivront par la foi. » \v 12 Mais la Loi n’est pas fondée sur la foi. La Loi dit : « Celui qui fait ces choses vivra en les faisant. »

ko.L: 율법으로는 아무도 하나님 앞에서 의롭다고 인정받지 못한다는 것이 분명합니다. "의인은 믿음으로 살 것이다" [하였기] 때문입니다. \v 12 그러나 율법은 믿음에서 [난 것이] 아닙니다. 오히려 "그것들을 행하는 사람은 그것들로 살 것이다" [하였습니다].
ko.B: 율법으로는 아무도 하나님 앞에서 의롭다고 인정받지 못한다는 것이 분명합니다. "의로운 사람은 믿음으로 살 것이다" 하였기 때문입니다. \v 12 그러나 율법은 믿음에 바탕을 두고 있지 않습니다. 오히려 "이것들을 행하는 사람은 그것으로 살 것이다" 하였습니다.
ko.R: 율법을 지켜서 하나님께 의롭다고 인정받을 사람이 아무도 없다는 것은 분명합니다. 성경은 "의로운 사람은 믿음으로 살 것이다" 하고 말합니다. \v 12 그러나 율법은 믿음에 바탕을 두지 않습니다. 율법은 "이것들을 행하는 사람은 그것을 행함으로써 살 것이다" 하고 말합니다.

vi.L: Và rõ ràng là không ai được xưng công chính trước mặt Đức Chúa Trời bởi luật pháp, vì: "Người công chính sẽ sống bởi đức tin." \v 12 Nhưng luật pháp không [đến] từ đức tin; trái lại: "Người nào làm những điều ấy sẽ sống bởi những điều ấy."
vi.B: Rõ ràng là không ai được xưng công chính trước mặt Đức Chúa Trời nhờ luật pháp, vì "Người công chính sẽ sống bởi đức tin." \v 12 Nhưng luật pháp không dựa trên đức tin. Trái lại, "Ai làm những điều này sẽ sống nhờ những điều ấy."
vi.R: Rõ ràng là không ai được Đức Chúa Trời công nhận là công chính nhờ giữ luật pháp. Kinh Thánh chép: "Người công chính sẽ sống bởi đức tin." \v 12 Nhưng luật pháp không dựa trên đức tin. Luật pháp nói: "Người nào làm những điều này sẽ sống nhờ làm những điều ấy."

pt.L: E que ninguém é justificado diante de Deus pela Lei [é] evidente, porque "O justo viverá pela fé." \v 12 Mas a Lei não é da fé; pelo contrário, "Aquele que as fizer viverá por elas."
pt.B: É claro que ninguém é declarado justo diante de Deus por meio da Lei, porque "Aquele que é justo viverá pela fé." \v 12 Mas a Lei não se baseia na fé. Ao contrário: "Quem fizer essas coisas viverá por elas."
pt.R: Está claro que ninguém é aceito por Deus como justo por cumprir a Lei. A Escritura diz: "A pessoa que é justa viverá pela fé." \v 12 Mas a Lei não se baseia na fé. A Lei diz: "A pessoa que fizer essas coisas viverá por fazê-las."

am.L: በሕግ ማንም በእግዚአብሔር ፊት እንደማይጸድቅ ግልጽ [ነው]፤ ምክንያቱም «ጻድቅ በእምነት በሕይወት ይኖራል።» \v 12 ሕግ ግን ከእምነት አይደለም፤ ይልቁንም «እነዚህን የሚያደርግ በእነርሱ በሕይወት ይኖራል።»
am.B: ማንም በሕግ በኩል በእግዚአብሔር ፊት እንደማይጸድቅ ግልጽ ነው፤ ምክንያቱም «ጻድቅ የሆነ በእምነት በሕይወት ይኖራል።» \v 12 ሕግ ግን በእምነት ላይ የተመሠረተ አይደለም። ይልቁንም «እነዚህን የሚያደርግ በእነርሱ በሕይወት ይኖራል።»
am.R: ሕጉን በመጠበቅ ማንም ከእግዚአብሔር ጋር ትክክለኛ ግንኙነት እንደማያገኝ ግልጽ ነው። መጽሐፍ እንዲህ ይላል፦ «ጻድቃን በእምነት በሕይወት ይኖራሉ።» \v 12 ሕጉ ግን በእምነት ላይ የተመሠረተ አይደለም። ሕጉ እንዲህ ይላል፦ «እነዚህን ነገሮች የሚያደርግ ሰው እነርሱን በማድረግ በሕይወት ይኖራል።»

decisions.choice: it is evident that no one is justified by the law, because the righteous will live by faith
alternatives: because no one is justified by the law, it is evident that the righteous will live by faith
decisions.reason: The sentence has two ὅτι clauses, and either can go with "evident". We take the first: the quotation from Habakkuk is the proof. The other reading makes the quotation the conclusion. Both say that a right standing with God comes by faith, not by the law.

decisions.choice: God declares a person to be in the right before him: acquitted and accepted
alternatives: a person proves to be good
decisions.reason: δικαιόω is a word from the law court: the judge declares someone to be in the right. Here God is the judge, and the person he justifies is accepted by him and stands in the right before him (2:16). It is a verdict God gives, not a reward for good conduct.

decisions.choice: a quotation of Habakkuk 2:4
decisions.reason: The words come from Habakkuk 2:4, where God tells the prophet that the righteous will live by faith while the proud fail. The Hebrew has "by his faithfulness" and the Greek translation "by my faith"; Paul quotes it without either word, as he does in Romans 1:17.

decisions.choice: the righteous will live by faith
alternatives: the one who is righteous by faith will live
decisions.reason: The phrase "by faith" can go with "live" or with "the righteous". Paul's argument is about how a person comes to be in the right, so the second reading is possible; but the order of the words follows Habakkuk, where it goes with "live". The meaning is close either way: righteousness and life come by faith.

decisions.choice: a quotation of Leviticus 18:5
alternatives: Paul's own summary of the law
decisions.reason: Leviticus 18:5 promises life to the one who does God's statutes. Paul sets it beside Habakkuk 2:4 to show that the law works by doing, while life with God comes by faith (compare Romans 10:5).

decisions.choice: the law is not of faith: it works on the principle of doing
alternatives: the law is opposed to faith or is evil
decisions.reason: Paul is not saying the law is bad (verse 21). He is saying that the law's basis is doing what it commands, which is a different basis from believing.

decisions.choice: justified (L, B); put right with God (R)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the legal word. Readable says what it means (meaning note m2).

decisions.choice: by keeping the law; Scripture says; The law says; by doing them
decisions.reason: Readable says how the law could be thought to justify, names the source of each quotation, and makes the last words plain.

decisions.choice: «El justo vivirá por [la] fe» (L); «El que es justo vivirá por la fe» (B); «La persona que es justa vivirá por la fe» (R)
alternatives: «Los que son justos vivirán por la fe» (R)
decisions.reason: Paul quotes Habakkuk 2:4 in the same words as in Romans 1:17, so the Spanish quotation is the same at each level as there. Readable keeps the singular of Romans where the English Readable has a plural; the sense is the same.

decisions.choice: "Mwenye haki ataishi kwa imani" (L); "Mtu aliye mwenye haki ataishi kwa imani" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Paul quotes Habakkuk 2:4 in the same words as in Romans 1:17, so the Swahili quotation is the same at each level as there. Leviticus 18:5 likewise follows Romans 10:5 ("ataishi kwa kuyafanya" in Readable).

decisions.choice: "의인" (L); "의로운 사람" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal uses the short word "의인" (a righteous person), close to the Greek's one word; Balanced and Readable say "의로운 사람", the plainer form used in Romans. Both keep the root "의". |

decisions.choice: "người công chính", "người nào", "ai", with no gender span
alternatives: a gender span as in the English
decisions.reason: Vietnamese "người" and "ai" include men and women, so the setting has nothing to change.

decisions.choice: O justo viverá pela fé (L); Aquele que é justo viverá pela fé (B); A pessoa que é justa viverá pela fé (R)
decisions.reason: Habakkuk 2:4 in the same words as Romans 1:17, so that readers recognise the one quotation in both letters.

decisions.choice: በሕይወት ይኖራል (will live, have life)
decisions.reason: On its own "ይኖራል" can mean "will stay" or "will dwell"; "በሕይወት" makes it plain that both quotations promise life.

source.text: Χριστὸς ἡμᾶς ἐξηγόρασεν ἐκ τῆς κατάρας τοῦ νόμου γενόμενος ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν κατάρα, ὅτι γέγραπται· Ἐπικατάρατος πᾶς ὁ κρεμάμενος ἐπὶ ξύλου, ἵνα εἰς τὰ ἔθνη ἡ εὐλογία τοῦ Ἀβραὰμ γένηται ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ, ἵνα τὴν ἐπαγγελίαν τοῦ πνεύματος λάβωμεν διὰ τῆς πίστεως.

records.literal_gloss: Christ us redeemed from the curse of the law, having become for us a curse, because it has been written: Cursed everyone the hanging on a tree, \v 14 so that to the Gentiles the blessing of the Abraham might come in Christ Jesus, so that the promise of the Spirit we might receive through the faith.

en.L: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} redeemed us from the curse of the law, having become a curse for us, because it is written, "Cursed [is] everyone who hangs on a tree," \v 14 so that the blessing of Abraham might come to the Gentiles in {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus, so that we might receive the promise of the Spirit through faith.
en.B: {{christos:Christ|The Messiah}} redeemed us from the curse of the law by becoming a curse on our behalf, for it is written, "A curse is on everyone who is hung on a tree." \v 14 He did this so that in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus the blessing of Abraham would reach the Gentiles, and so that through faith we would receive the Spirit who was promised.
en.R: {{christos:Christ|The Messiah}} paid the price to set us free from the curse that the law brings. He did it by taking the curse on {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} for us. Scripture says, "Everyone who is hung on a tree is under a curse." \v 14 He did this so that the blessing God promised to Abraham would come to the Gentiles through {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus. And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did it so that we would receive the Spirit God promised, through faith.
